nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of this analysis on sustainable plastics behaviours in the EU?
nodes.answer: This analysis is the first EU cross-country comparison of sustainable plastics behaviours, providing insights into a wide range of consumer behaviours in the region.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some common theoretical models used in studies related to plastic sustainable consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: Some common theoretical models used in studies related to plastic sustainable consumer behaviour are the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), Norm-Activation theory (NAM), and Value-Belief-Norm theory (VBN).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do factors like environmental concern, risk perception, contextual factors, and habits influence plastic sustainable consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: Factors like environmental concern, risk perception, contextual factors, and habits have been found to influence plastic sustainable consumer behaviour according to Nova et al. (2022) and other studies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Which model in the regression analysis results demonstrates the highest predictive power for sustainable plastics consumption behaviour?
nodes.answer: Model 4, for sustainable plastics consumption behaviour, explains 42% of the variance, indicating higher predictive power compared to other models.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How does gender factor into the regression analysis results for sustainable plastics behaviours?
nodes.answer: Gender (female) has a positive coefficient in all models, indicating that being female is associated with higher levels of sustainable behaviour.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some personal factors that influence individual plastic packaging consumption according to the focus group discussions with German consumers?
nodes.answer: The personal factors that influence individual plastic packaging consumption include convenience, lifestyle preferences, habits, and perceived benefits of using plastic packaging.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Plastic-free product preference_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do personal factors such as convenience and lifestyle preferences impact individual plastic packaging consumption?
nodes.answer: Convenience and lifestyle preferences can lead individuals to choose products with excessive plastic packaging, opt for single-use plastic items, and prioritize convenience over sustainability, thus contributing to higher plastic consumption.
